Improvement of the disease inflammations , rheumatoid , rheumatic fever , trauma , tumors Ill, Why ESR is increased in these conditions 7 ESR is a sensitive indicator of tissue damage. In these conditions , there is an increase in the level of fibrinogen which causes RBCs to aggregate. Aggregated RBCs have greater density than plasma so they sediment (settle) faster with the effect of gravity. Clinical importance/significance of ESR Advantage: easy and cheap but non-specific i.e. raised ESR does not indicate a particular disease but its decrease indicates improvement of the condition. ocrText: = Female Urethra: - It is about 4 cm long extending from the internal to the external urethral orifices - Itis wider and more dilatable than male urethra - It begins from the bladder neck at the internal urethral orifice, and descends downwards and forwards, traversing the deep and superficial perineal pouches - It ends by the external urethral orifice into the vestibule of the vagina between the clitoris and the vaginal opening. - It's upper (initial) part: surrounded by the sphincter urethrae - It is connected to inferior part of pubic bone by pubovesical ligament - Relations of female urethra: Anteriorly: separated from symphysis pubis by fat Posteriorly: adherent to the anterior wall of the 30 vagina 2 ١ j Ureter - ٠ Itis an exclusively a passage for urine lined by bd transitional epithelium at the initial part then 3 stratified squamous epithelium ١ 8 ١ . j * The lamina propria of the female urethra is » 1 f highly vascular : 1/14 ‏للا‎ ‎* It contains the openings of ducts of the Urethra mucus-secreting urethral glands of Littré = Development of kidney: Primordia: Intermediate mass of mesoderm: - Inthe cervical part, it is segmented into groups of cells called nephrotomes - Inthe caudal part, it gives a longitudinal ridge called nephrogenic - Three sets of kidneys appear following each other: Pronephros, Mesonephros, Metanephros 97 1. Pronephros: Most primitive Kidney - The cervical nephrotomes give 5-7 pairs of pronephric tubules which open in a duct called pronephric duct ‏ل‎ Sm sen ge na, - The pronephros are non-functioning in 86 i i mammals K ٠. H - The tubules degenerate by the 4th week. - Pronephric duct persists to become the ik J mesonephric duct i ot 2. Mesonephros - Itis formed of about 80 mesonephric tubules - Itdiffers from pronephros in the following: * The mesonephric tubules are more caudal and more numerous (80). ٠ They have no special duct, they use the pronephric duct which is now called mesonephric duct (Wolffian duct) - The mesonephric duct elongates and opens into the cloaca - Each mesonephric tubule has 2 ends; one end opens in the mesonephric duct while the other end differentiates into a cup-shaped Bowman's capsule that is invaginated by capillaries forming the Glomerulus - Bowman's capsule and Glomerulus make up the Renal Corpuscle - Mesonephric kidney functions for sometime and then degenerates. - Some mesonephric tubules persist and give efferent ductulus in males while in female, they give epophoron and parophoron - The mesonephric duct forms the epididymis, vas deferens and ejaculatory duct in males while it disappears in females leaving Gartner's duct. 3. Metanephros: It is the permanent kidney - It begins functioning at 9 weeks - Urine is produced and released into amniotic fluid 98

ocrText: | Milk | ‏هه‎ Composition:- 1. Carbohydrates: e The only carbohydrate present in milk is Lactose disaccharide. e Itis formed by mammary gland from blood glucose. e It is less sweet (there won't be vomiting in case of excessive intake of milk by infant from mother). e Less liable to fermentation, Laxative (prevent constipation). e In presence of bacteria, it is converted to Lactic acid. 2. Minerals: e Most of minerals especially Calcium and Phosphorus. ‏ش‎ ‎e Milk is poor in Copper and Iron. 3. ocrText: The anterior abdominal wall of a 21-year-old woman impacts the steering wheel during a head-on car collision. The blunt trauma resulted in a lacerated pancreas with digestive enzyme spilling anterior. Which of the following locations would initially receive the contents of the lacerated pancreas? A. Supracolic part of greater peritoneal sac B. Infracolic part of greater peritoneal sac Cc. Subhepatic space D. Omental bursa ‏.ع‎ Subphrenic space © camscanner The answer is D: Omental bursa. ¢ The omental bursa (or lesser peritoneal sac) is an isolated part of the peritoneal cavity. which lies posterior to the stomach and antenor to the pancreas. Because of its location. the omental bursa would receive digestive enzymes emanating | from the lacerated section of the anterior pancreas. The only connection between the omental bursa and the remaining aspects of the peritoneal cavity is through the epiploic (omental) foramen. © camscanner

ocrText: Neoplasia a INTRODUCTION ٠ the term ‘neoplasia’ means new growth; the new growth produced is called ‘neoplasm’ or ‘tumour’. ‏ها‎ Scientific Definition of a neoplasm or tumour : > mass of tissue formed as result of abnormal, excessive, uncoordinated, autonomous and purposeless proliferation of cells even after cessation of stimulus for growth which caused it’. - Uncoordinated :badly organized - Purposeless : have no value or use - Autonomous : act independently , loss of control and regulation of replication - Neoplasms may be: © benign: when they are slow-growing and localized without causing much difficulty to the host. © malignant : when they are rapidly-growing , spread throughout body and may eventually cause death of host. 18 Oncology (oncos=tumour, logos=study) :branch of science dealing with the study of neoplasms or tumors QO Basic components of any tumors benign \ malignant: 1- Parenchyma ; comprised by proliferating tumor cells, parenchyma determines the nature and evolution of the tumor. 2- Supportive stroma : composed of fibrous CT and blood vessels; it provides the framework on which the parenchymal tumor cells grow. O Origin of cancer cells : — Cancer cells originate by clonal proliferation of a single progeny of a cell (monoclonality). - Cancer cells arise from stem cells ,characterized by : prolonged self-renewal and asymmetric replication and trans-differentiation . O Nomenclature of benign tumors: > The suffix ‘-oma’ is added to denote benign tumors. > Add Sarcoma: (sarcos = fleshy) Malignant tumors originating from mesenchymal origin . > Add Carcinoma: (carcin = hard) Malignant tumors originating from epithelial origin. > Exceptions : - Melanoma \ carcinoma of the melanocytes. —Hepatoma \ carcinoma of the hepatocytes, —Lymphoma \ malignant tumor of the lymphoid tissue, —Seminoma \ malignant tumor of the testis. — Leukaemia \ malignant tumor of blood forming cells. O Classification of tumors is based on: — Epithelial, — Benign , malignant, borderline ,or locally malignant — Mesenchymal, — Primary or secondary — Hematopoietic, - Clinical features, - Germ cell tumors. - Morphological characteristics 1. Mixed tumors: When two types of tumors are combined in the same tumor. e.g. - Adenosquamous carcinoma , Adenoacanthoma, Carcinosarcoma - Mixed tumour of the salivary gland (or pleomorphic adenoma) benign tumour having combination of both epithelial and mesenchymal tissue elements. 2- Teratomas: tumors arising from totipotent cells derived from the three germ cell layers; ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm. - Most common sites for teratomas are ovaries and testis (gonadal teratomas). 3. Hamartoma: - benign tumor which is made of mature but disorganized cells of tissues indigenous to particular organ e.g. hamartoma of the lung consists of mature cartilage, mature smooth muscle and epithelium. 4. Choristoma: heterotopia but is not a true tumor, composed of ectopic islan iormal tissue. pathology - neoplasia mScamner
